exercises.instruction: 17–18 Express $$D$$ as a region of type I and also as a region of type II. Then evaluate the double integral in two ways.

problem.paragraph: $$\iint\limits_{D}{x\mathit{dA}, D}$$ is enclosed by the lines $$y = x$$ , $$y = 0$$ , $$x = 1$$

solution.paragraph: Type I: $$D = \left\{ \left( {x,y} \right) \middle| 0 \leqslant x \leqslant 1,0 \leqslant y \leqslant x \right\}$$ , type II: $$D = \left\{ \left( {x,y} \right) \middle| 0 \leqslant y \leqslant 1,y \leqslant x \leqslant 1 \right\}$$ ; $$\frac{1}{3}$$

image.alt: Details A surface and a shaded region are graphed in the first octant of the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The positive x and y axes have a single tick mark labeled 1. The surface resembles a saddle. Imagine a rectangular plane parallel to the x y plane. Its back left corner is on the positive z axis and its front right corner is elevated higher than the back left corner. The plane is bent concave up diagonally from the back left corner to the front right corner and diagonally concave down from the front left corner to the back right corner. The shaded region, labeled D, lies on the x y plane and is triangular with its vertices at (0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), and (1, 1, 0).

Details A surface and a shaded region are graphed in the first octant of the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The positive x and y axes have a single tick mark labeled 1. The surface is a part of a paraboloid, labeled z = x^2 + y^2 with its vertex at the origin. The surface is the quarter of the paraboloid in the first octant. The shaded region lies on the x y plane and is bound by a curve, a line, and the positive x axis. The curve is labeled y = x^2, z = 0, begins from the origin and traces a parabolic path in the first quadrant of the x y plane, opening down to the right, parallel to the y axis. The line runs parallel to the positive y axis from the tick mark 1 on the positive x axis and meets the curve. The region bound by the curve, the line and the positive x axis is shaded and labeled D.

exercises.instruction: 80–81 Mean Value Theorem for Double Integrals The Mean Value Theorem for double integrals says that if $$f$$ is a continuous function on a plane region $$D$$ that is of type I or type II, then there exists a point $$\left( x_{0},y_{0} \right)$$ in $$D$$ such that $$\iint\limits_{D}f\left( {x,y} \right)\mathit{dA} = f(x_{0},y_{0})A(D)$$
